purpose: Additional primary-source assumption check accompanying the five implemented experiments. This supplements earlier research; it neither claims exhaustive coverage nor adds new solver runs.
interpretation: Findings paraphrase cited sources. Transfer limits and ourInference are our critical assessment, not claims made by their authors. None of these papers certifies the experimental code or its PCB outputs.

sources.title: Searching with Consistent Prioritization for Multi-Agent Path Finding
sources.read: Full theoretical section and algorithm framing
sources.finding: Conflict-driven search over partial priorities can improve prioritized planning. The paper also proves general incompleteness and suboptimality, including sensitivity to equally good individual path choices.
sources.transferLimit: The model contains moving agents and time; PCB copper remains in place. Its guarantees do not certify this bounded finite-width, multilayer router.
sources.ourInference: Searching priority orders cannot substitute for testing alternative physical witnesses. The accepted prior-witness move is useful mechanism evidence, while the soft-only ablation is needed to attribute the bundle's benefit.

sources.title: Multi-Agent Path Finding with Continuous Time and Geometric Agents Viewed through Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT)
sources.finding: Lazy conflict generation extends an SMT encoding when geometric agent conflicts are discovered.
sources.transferLimit: Circular moving agents on predefined straight-line connections differ from permanent copper, drilled vias and board ownership. The short publication does not validate our candidate archive.
sources.ourInference: Conditional conflict facts are a reasonable design pattern, but domain exhaustion only rejects the archived candidates. It does not prove the physical board unroutable.

sources.title: FLUTE: Fast Lookup Table Based Rectilinear Steiner Minimal Tree Algorithm for VLSI Design
sources.finding: Lookup-table Steiner construction optimizes rectilinear tree length for low-degree nets, with decomposition for larger nets.
sources.transferLimit: A short abstract tree is not a routed, finite-width, obstacle-avoiding PCB tree. It does not account for all later interactions created by fixing copper.
sources.ourInference: Forest sharing can reduce demand and drills yet worsen global routability. Eligibility and downstream effects must be measured instead of treating tree length as the final objective.

sources.title: FastRoute 4.0: Global Router with Efficient Via Minimization
sources.read: Author-hosted indexed text covering overview and via-aware tree construction; direct PDF fetch rejected
sources.finding: The flow combines via-aware trees, bounded pattern routing, congestion handling and ordered layer assignment rather than relying only on a via penalty in maze routing.
sources.transferLimit: The global grid-capacity model and preferred-direction layers differ from this PCB pipeline's exact copper. Reported contest improvements cannot be transferred numerically.
sources.ourInference: The forest result argues for evaluating sharing together with congestion and future layer cost. Committing geometrically valid copper too early can trade fewer demands for more difficult remaining routes.

sources.title: Algorithms for Routing and Testing Routability of Planar VLSI Layouts
sources.finding: For a supplied planar layout sketch, topology and feature positions support routability testing and wire-length optimization through a rubber-band representation.
sources.transferLimit: A fixed one-layer rectilinear sketch is narrower than multilayer PCB routing with irregular pads, width changes and vias. Preserving order alone does not certify that broader problem.
sources.ourInference: Constructive local witnesses improve the portal experiment's evidence, but the remaining certified cells must be profiled before assuming witness replay removes expensive global search.

sources.title: A “Greedy” Channel Router
sources.read: Author-hosted indexed algorithm and density discussion
sources.finding: Channel density supplies a width lower bound, while vertical conflicts and routing choices still affect feasibility and via/length tradeoffs.
sources.transferLimit: The algorithm may add tracks or route outside the channel ends to succeed. A fixed PCB region cannot assume those extra resources. Its track model does not directly certify arbitrary board regions.
sources.ourInference: Crossing counts and point spacing are limited surrogate objectives. An inactive later refinement does not reject earlier joint incidence or layer planning.

sources.title: Rectilinear Shortest Paths and Minimum Spanning Trees in the Presence of Rectilinear Obstacles
sources.finding: Obstacle- and terminal-induced track graphs support efficient shortest-path and spanning-tree searches under a rectilinear model.
sources.transferLimit: The theorem depends on the graph and obstacle model. The experiment has rotated shapes, finite widths, permanent traces, vias and explicitly bounded event generation.
sources.ourInference: Restricted-graph exhaustion and query-cap exhaustion are implementation outcomes, not proofs of physical impossibility. Simple direct-routing wins should remain separate from full replacement claims.

sources.title: A Matching-Based Escape Routing Algorithm With Variable Design Rules and Multiple Constraints
sources.read: Publisher abstract and bibliographic metadata; full method not independently reproduced
sources.finding: The reported escape-routing flow combines obstacle-aware pin projection, hierarchical sequencing, global congestion optimization and detailed routing with variable rules.
sources.transferLimit: Its reported industrial escape instances are not our full-board populations. The abstract alone does not disclose enough to reproduce its performance or certify its baselines.
sources.ourInference: Early escape sequencing remains plausible. The zero accepted decisions in our later planner constitute a narrow implementation nonwin, not a rejection of that broader research direction.

sources.title: Two stage Ordered Escape Routing combined with LP and heuristic algorithm for large scaled PCB
sources.read: Publisher indexed abstract/highlights; direct full-page retrieval rejected
sources.finding: The described method combines a multicommodity-flow/linear-programming stage with heuristic congestion handling for ordered escape routing.
sources.transferLimit: Relaxed flow is not an exact finite-width copper certificate, and escape routing is not an end-to-end whole-board benchmark.
sources.ourInference: This is a resource for an earlier decision formulation, not evidence that adding another optimizer after the current pathing stage would help.

sources.title: PCBWorld: A Benchmark Environment for Engine-Grounded PCB Design Automation
sources.read: Primary full-text environment/actions, evaluation, check catalog and rollout-selection descriptions; public repository metadata verified
sources.finding: Engine-native operations and independent completed-board evaluation connect routing actions to actual geometric checks. The release includes synthetic and real-board data; main results distinguish selected rollouts from single-rollout outcomes.
sources.transferLimit: The engine, input format, rule catalog, supported actions and rollout budgets differ from our pinned SRJ/360-second protocol. This study is not a head-to-head evaluation of our solvers.
sources.ourInference: It is a useful future external validation resource. Its emphasis on connectivity plus checks supports keeping completion, full-copper findings, style and runtime distinct; no requested benchmark is replaced here.

sources.title: Routing Dense Layouts with History-Aware Offline Reinforcement Learning using LSTM
sources.read: Primary full-text methodology, controls, training/evaluation split and result tables
sources.finding: An iteration-level learned controller changes four existing cost knobs in OpenROAD. The paper evaluates unseen density/adjustment settings on designs also present during training; hard cases can retain violations despite large reductions.
sources.transferLimit: These are IC detailed-routing experiments with router-specific features and substantial training. They do not show transfer to unseen PCB designs or a guaranteed clean solution.
sources.ourInference: Cost calibration can matter without replacing search. Our cheap deterministic pricing ablation should establish its own effect and quality limits before a learned controller adds complexity.

sources.title: OmniRouting: A Semantic-Coupled Multimodal Benchmark for Constraint-Aware Spatial Reasoning in PCB Routing
sources.read: Primary abstract and release statement only
sources.finding: The proposed benchmark jointly considers geometric rules, connectivity and schematic semantics in PCB routing.
sources.transferLimit: The inspected abstract promises a future open-source release; data and evaluator availability were not independently established. Its claims are not used as measured evidence here.
sources.ourInference: Useful context for evaluating representation/identity loss, but not a runnable substitute for the requested datasets or an independently verified solver improvement.

implementationObservationsNotNewMeasured.observation: The zero-factor pricing mode still calculates the nearest future point before multiplying by zero. A zero-factor fast path is a possible implementation simplification; it was not implemented or benchmarked in this campaign.
implementationObservationsNotNewMeasured.limit: This does not alter or invalidate the measured c57 mode; no speedup is attributed to an unimplemented shortcut. Hard future-segment checks remain a separate policy.
